name: scenario
value: How much expansion capital should an enterprise actually commit?

name: method
value: An initial Year 0 investment followed by equal annual net flows. Benefits fall and operating costs rise under the selected stress assumption. NPV includes Year 0; IRR is the discount rate at which NPV is zero.

name: formula
value: Annual net flow = benefit × (1 − stress) − operating cost × (1 + stress/2). NPV = −investment + Σ(net flow/(1+r)^year). IRR solves NPV = 0 for this conventional cash-flow pattern.

name: limits
value: Synthetic flows exclude residual value, taxes, replacement costs, inflation, financing and shadow-price adjustments. Public/private context does not by itself establish ENPV/FNPV or EIRR/FIRR. Generic NPV and IRR describe only the entered demonstration flows.

name: parameter_origin
value: Case-specific investment, benefit, operating cost, years and default discount rate from the original prototype; no underlying project accounts supplied.

name: calibration
value: None supplied; no fitted coefficients or observed outcome dataset
